title: MATH GAOKAO - 371
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Imaginary Part of a Complex Number
questions.learningObjective: Identify the imaginary part of a complex number in standard form.
questions.question: For \(z=2-5i\), find \(\operatorname{Im}(z)\).
questions.explanation: A complex number in standard form is \(a+bi\), where \(\operatorname{Im}(z)=b\). For \(z=2-5i\), the coefficient of \(i\) is \(-5\), so \(\operatorname{Im}(z)=-5\). Thus the correct option is B.
questions.hint: In \(a+bi\), the imaginary part is the coefficient of \(i\), including its sign.

questions.concept: Real Part of a Complex Number
questions.learningObjective: Identify the real part of a complex number in standard form.
questions.question: For \(z=-3+7i\), find \(\operatorname{Re}(z)\).
questions.explanation: In the standard form \(a+bi\), the real part is \(a\). For \(z=-3+7i\), the real part is \(-3\). Thus the correct option is B.
questions.hint: In \(a+bi\), the real part is the term without \(i\).

questions.concept: Real and Imaginary Parts after Subtraction
questions.learningObjective: Compute a difference of complex numbers and identify its imaginary part.
questions.question: If \(z=(2+3i)-(4-i)\), find \(\operatorname{Im}(z)\).
questions.explanation:
Subtract the complex numbers:
\[
\begin{aligned}
z&=(2+3i)-(4-i) \\
&=2+3i-4+i \\
&=-2+4i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Im}(z)=4\). Therefore the correct option is B.
questions.hint: Combine real parts and imaginary parts separately, then read the coefficient of \(i\).

questions.learningObjective: Multiply complex numbers and identify the imaginary part of the result.
questions.question: If \(z=(3+2i)(1-i)\), find \(\operatorname{Im}(z)\).
questions.explanation:
Expand the product:
\[
z=(3+2i)(1-i)=3-3i+2i-2i^2.
\]
Since \(i^2=-1\),
\[
z=3-i+2=5-i.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Im}(z)=-1\). Therefore the correct option is A.
questions.hint: Expand the product and use \(i^2=-1\), then identify the coefficient of \(i\).

questions.learningObjective: Square a complex number and identify the real part of the result.
questions.question: If \(z=2+3i\), find \(\operatorname{Re}(z^2)\).
questions.explanation:
Compute the square:
\[
z^2=(2+3i)^2=4+12i+9i^2.
\]
Since \(i^2=-1\),
\[
z^2=4+12i-9=-5+12i.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Re}(z^2)=-5\). Therefore the correct option is B.

questions.concept: Imaginary Part after Combining Square and Conjugate
questions.learningObjective: Compute an expression involving a square and a conjugate, then identify its imaginary part.
questions.question: If \(z=1+i\), find \(\operatorname{Im}(z^2+\overline{z})\).
questions.explanation:
First compute
\[
\begin{aligned}
z^2&=(1+i)^2 \\
&=1+2i+i^2 \\
&=2i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Also,
\[
\overline{z}=1-i.
\]
Therefore,
\[
z^2+\overline{z}=2i+(1-i)=1+i.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Im}(z^2+\overline{z})=1\). Therefore the correct option is B.
questions.hint: Compute \(z^2\) and \(\overline{z}\) separately, then add them.

questions.learningObjective: Use a complex equation to determine the real part of an unknown complex number.
questions.question: If \(z=a+bi\), \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(2z-\overline{z}=3+4i\), find \(a\).
questions.explanation:
Since \(z=a+bi\) and \(\overline{z}=a-bi\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
2z-\overline{z}&=2(a+bi)-(a-bi) \\
&=2a+2bi-a+bi \\
&=a+3bi.
\end{aligned}
\]
Given \(2z-\overline{z}=3+4i\), compare real and imaginary parts:
\[
a=3,\qquad 3b=4.
\]
Thus \(a=3\). Therefore the correct option is A.
questions.hint: Express \(z\) and \(\overline{z}\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\), then compare real parts.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a quotient of complex numbers and identify its imaginary part.
questions.question: If \(z=\frac{1+i}{1-i}\), find \(\operatorname{Im}(z)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(1+i\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
z&=\frac{1+i}{1-i}\cdot\frac{1+i}{1+i} \\
&=\frac{(1+i)^2}{1^2-i^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Now \((1+i)^2=1+2i+i^2=2i\), and \(1^2-i^2=1-(-1)=2\). Hence
\[
z=\frac{2i}{2}=i.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Im}(z)=1\). Therefore the correct option is A.
questions.hint: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a power of a complex number and identify its real part.
questions.question: If \(z=2-i\), find \(\operatorname{Re}(z^3)\).
questions.explanation:
First compute
\[
\begin{aligned}
z^2&=(2-i)^2 \\
&=4-4i+i^2 \\
&=3-4i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then
\[
z^3=z\cdot z^2=(2-i)(3-4i).
\]
Expanding,
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2-i)(3-4i)&=6-8i-3i+4i^2 \\
&=6-11i-4 \\
&=2-11i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Re}(z^3)=2\). Therefore the correct option is A.
questions.hint: Compute \(z^2\) first, then multiply by \(z\) and simplify.

questions.learningObjective: Use a complex equation to determine the imaginary part of an unknown complex number.
questions.question: If \(z=x+yi\), \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(z+2\overline{z}=6-3i\), find \(y\).
questions.explanation:
Since \(z=x+yi\) and \(\overline{z}=x-yi\),
\[
z+2\overline{z}=x+yi+2(x-yi)=3x-yi.
\]
Given \(z+2\overline{z}=6-3i\), compare real and imaginary parts:
\[
3x=6,\qquad -y=-3.
\]
Thus \(x=2\) and \(y=3\). Therefore the correct option is B.
questions.hint: Write \(z\) and \(\overline{z}\) in terms of \(x\) and \(y\), then compare imaginary parts.
